In one minute
  • Read this as a workbench, not a verdict. 10.5% of the registry is still empty, and the CEAGI accountability score is still work in progress - no ranking is published yet (see the To-do list).
  • The campaign is crowded: 20 of 21 policy themes are claimed by two or more parties, and USFP and PPS overlap on 17 of them.
  • The most crowded theme is Social protection & pensions, claimed by 8 of 9 parties.
  • All 72 campaign claims carry a grade, but 19 still rest on a single source, so they are not corroborated under the project's own rule.
  • In 2021 Istiqlal was the most over-represented party (advantage ratio 1.15) and PSU the most under-represented (0.30): the seat formula did not turn votes into seats evenly.

2. How every grade in this report is decided

Nothing here is a black box. Each claim carries a class (what kind of commitment it is) and a verification score (how checkable it is), both stored in data/claims.csv; each source carries a confidence level and a reliability score. The tables below are the exact rules, and the last column shows how many of this year's 72 campaign claims fall in each bucket.

Class - what kind of commitment is it?

ClassNameThe ruleWeight2026 claims
QQuantifieda target with a number and a unit1.042
VDirectionala commitment in principle, with no number0.430
SSlogan / identitya value statement, not a measurable promise0.10
NNegative / attacka criticism of a rival, not an offer0.20

The class sets how much the claim counts in the credibility sub-index C: a quantified target counts fully, a vague commitment about 40%, a slogan about 10%.

Verification score - how checkable is it?

ScoreNameWhat it requires2026 claims
1/5Unverifiableno baseline, no unit, no deadline30
2/5Weaka target, but a missing baseline or deadline, and/or a single source41
3/5Moderatecomplete, but single-source or contested1
4/5Strongcomplete, corroborated by 2+ independent sources, feasible0
5/5Auditedindependently verified by a neutral body0

Today no claim scores above 2, because most baseline cells are still FILL: the rubric ties a higher score to completeness (target + baseline + deadline). That is why the credibility sub-index is low for every party - it is a statement about the evidence, not about the party.

Confidence - how solid is the sourcing?

LevelMeaning
HIGHofficial or verified, with corroborating sources
MEDIUMone solid source
LOWestimate or headline-only capture, still to verify
ILLUSTRATIVEplaceholder that demonstrates the pipeline - never cite

Corroboration - the project's own rule

A claim is called corroborated only when two or more independent sources carry it. In this campaign, 0 claims have no source linked, 19 rest on a single source (so they are not corroborated), 51 have two, and 2 have three or more.

What a score does not mean

  • Not a prediction. A high CEAGI does not mean a party will keep its promises; it means its promises are better evidenced and its record better documented.
  • Not a judgement of the policy. We grade whether a claim can be checked, not whether it is wise, affordable or desirable.
  • Not comparable across different coverage. Where a sub-index is missing it is shown as n/a and never guessed.

Glossary

CEAGI
Composite Electoral Accountability & Governance Index - this project's six-dimension score. It measures how evidenced a party's promises are and how well documented its record is, not how good its policies are.
Sub-index
One of the six dimensions D, C, E, G, L, M. Each is normalised to 0-1; a dimension with no evidence is shown as n/a.
Claim
A single promise or commitment taken from a party programme - one per row in data/claims.csv.
Quantified (Q)
A claim with a number and a unit, e.g. 'raise the minimum wage to 5,000 dirhams'.
Verification score
A 1-5 grade of how checkable a claim is: 1 = unverifiable, 5 = independently audited.
Corroborated
Carried by at least two independent sources. A claim resting on one source is not corroborated under this project's rule.
Confidence
How solid the sourcing is: HIGH, MEDIUM, LOW or ILLUSTRATIVE.
FILL
A cell the registry does not have yet. It is printed, not hidden, so the hole stays visible.
n/a
Not computable from the evidence. It is never replaced by a guess or by zero.
Quotient électoral
The electoral quota. In Moroccan law it is the number of registered voters in a constituency divided by the seats allocated to it.
Plus fort reste
Largest remainder - the rule that assigns the seats left over after the quota to the lists with the largest remainders.
Circonscription
A voting district (constituency). 305 seats are filled in local constituencies and 90 in the twelve regional ones.
AMO
Assurance Maladie Obligatoire - Morocco's compulsory health insurance.
Promise ledger
The record of what parties promised in past terms and what happened (fulfilled, partial, failed, still open).

3. Legal basis - what the law actually says

The seat arithmetic in the charts and the simulator comes from Morocco's organic law, not from convention. The text in force is loi organique n° 27.11 on the House of Representatives, consolidated on 29 January 2026 and amended most recently by loi organique n° 53.25 (January 2026), and before that by n° 04.21 (2021) and n° 20.16 (2016). Two articles carry the arithmetic that decides the 395 seats:

What this means in practice

  • 395 seats, two levels. 305 members are elected in local constituencies and 90 in regional constituencies; the law fixes the 90 regional seats in a table across the twelve regions.
  • Proportional, largest remainder. Seats go to lists in proportion to their support, and the seats left over after the quota go to the lists with the largest remainders.
  • The quota is based on registered voters, not votes cast. That is the distinctive Moroccan rule. In practice few lists reach the quota, so most seats are decided at the largest-remainder step.
  • No electoral threshold. The 3%/6% threshold that applied from 2002 to 2016 was removed by the 2021 reform; the current law sets none.
  • The former national list is gone. The 90 seats that used to be elected on a single national list are now elected in the regional constituencies.

The interactive seat simulator on this site applies the largest-remainder method to national vote totals that you enter. It is an illustration at national level: the real count runs constituency by constituency, on the registered-voter quotient. Read it with that in mind.

8. Claim convergence - who is promising the same thing

117 claims from 9 parties are tagged onto 21 policy themes. Where two or more parties land on the same theme, their programmes overlap - the promise is duplicated even when the wording is not. The single most crowded theme is Social protection & pensions: 8 of 9 parties (PPS, USFP, Istiqlal, RNI, PAM, MP, UC, Alliance de la gauche) each carry at least one claim on it.

Method: every claim is mapped to one or more themes in data/claim_themes.csv, an explicit editorial layer whose rows quote the phrase in the claim that justifies the tag. The controlled vocabulary is data/themes.csv. Nothing is inferred by keyword at build time; change the CSV and the picture changes. A theme is shared when two or more parties claim it, alone when only one does.

9. What CEAGI measures

CEAGI is this project's own yardstick, not an external rating agency. Its definition is written down once, in METHODOLOGY.md, and quoted here in full:

Six things make it up — D delivery of the 2021 promises, C promise credibility, E electoral efficiency, G governance, L leadership, M mandate coherence — and because they are multiplied together, a party that fails one cannot buy its way back with the others. Where a dimension has no evidence it is shown as n/a and never guessed: the score measures how evidenced and how well documented a party's record is, not whether its policies are good.

Work in progress. No CEAGI scores or ranking are shown in this report yet: scoring is deliberately withheld until every party has a complete, well-evidenced six-dimension record. Finishing it is on the To-do list below. The full algebra is in METHODOLOGY.md.

12. What the data supports, and what it does not

Supportable today

  • In 2021, Istiqlal was the most over-represented party (advantage ratio 1.15) and PSU the most under-represented (0.30) - the PR formula did not convert votes into seats evenly.
  • 72 campaign claims are registered for 2026, 72 of them scored and 53 corroborated. The most crowded domains are Water Security (2), Digital Transitionning (2), Identity + Amazigh (2).
  • 35 claims from the 2021 campaign(s) are recorded in the historical claims bank (not scored in the CEAGI model).

Not supportable yet

  • Delivery D is unavailable for 57 of 59 parties (Istiqlal, PJD, USFP, MP, PPS, UC ...). Scoring requires at least 3 concluded promises per party; the outgoing term's promises are still open, so its record cannot be judged yet.
  • Electoral efficiency E is missing for some parties: there is no 2021 election row for them.

15. Methodology (short)

Sources to facts/claims to synthesis. A claim is "corroborated" only with 2+ independent reliable sources. Delivery D = (fulfilled + 0.5·partial) / (fulfilled + partial + failed + abandoned), computed over completed terms only, and requires at least 3 concluded promises before it is scored at all. Credibility C = Σ(weight·rubric) / 5Σweight with class weights Q=1.0, V=0.4, S=0.1, N=0.2. Electoral efficiency E = 1 - |A-1| / max|A-1| where A = seat share / vote share for the 2021 election. Aggregation is a weighted geometric mean; uncertainty is 8,000 Monte-Carlo draws at σ=0.05. Full derivation in morocco-elections.org; per-number provenance in output/audit_trail.md.
